headline: Every bottle of flavour checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
visitLine: Call and visit to Carrum Downs
heroLede: Michaelona is a family-owned Melbourne company, established in 2000, that makes flavours, colours, seasonings and fragrances at Carrum Downs and supplies food makers here and overseas from SQF-approved premises. With hundreds of flavours going into similar containers, the label is what tells your customer what they are adding to their product. This is what a camera check could look like on a filling line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bottle has its cap on, straight and fully closed. A loose cap means a leak in the carton and a complaint from the customer.
labelLede: A vanilla and a hazelnut flavour can look the same in the bottle, and the wrong one can put an allergen into your customer’s product. The camera checks every bottle carries the right label for the run, straight and intact.
codeLede: The best-before and batch code has to be right and readable on every bottle. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the flavour and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Cap offcuts, label backing and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four crooked caps in fifteen minutes. Check the capper.
